And then there's the current Major Order as of writing this, kill 60,000,000 radicals in ~3 days.

To be honest this might have been possible but after the last 2 Major Order upsets, I think people just don't care.

A Game I Love, but One That Continues to Disappoint

I genuinely love Helldivers 2. Few games have managed to capture the same sense of teamwork, chaos, humor, and sheer enjoyment. At its best, it's one of the most entertaining multiplayer experiences I've ever had, which makes its current state all the more frustrating.

Since the latest update, stability has become a serious issue, and it's increasingly difficult to overlook problems that should have been addressed long ago. What makes this worse is the lack of consistent communication from Arrowhead and the apparent inability to deliver meaningful, lasting improvements despite having had so much time to address these issues.

I understand that game development is complicated and that updates can introduce unexpected problems. However, there comes a point where patience turns into frustration. Players shouldn't have to constantly wonder whether the next update will actually improve the experience or introduce another round of technical issues.

What disappoints me most is how much potential this game has. The foundation is incredible, the community is passionate, and the gameplay is genuinely special. Yet it feels like the developers continuously struggle to maintain the quality of the experience they've created.

I don't want Helldivers 2 to fail. Quite the opposite. I want it to succeed because I genuinely love this game. But loving something doesn't mean ignoring its shortcomings, and after this much time, I think it's reasonable to expect better stability, clearer communication, and more consistent progress.

I want to recommend this game, but in its current state, I simply can't.

I absolutely loved this game, I purchased the super citizen edition the first week it came out when you had to wait for hours in queue just to get in due to how full the servers were at the time. I would have considered this one of the best games that I have ever played but after everything that I have experienced and seen from the developers I can not even bear to recommend this game to anyone that I know, as it is a shell of the game it used to be. In the beginning it was so much fun, I got to meet a lot of really kind people and play a incredibly unique game that was nothing like anything that I have ever played before and I loved every single second that I spent playing at that time. Although there were a few bugs here and there the game was really fresh and it seemed like they were working on fixing it as well. Sadly this was not the case and in fact has appeared to get worse and worse with every single update. Stratagem bouncing and the hellpod controls still have not been fixed at all and seemingly, it seems like they have not even glanced at it either. Honestly I have seen so many bugs this late into development (two, close to 3 years old already) that should have been fixed and yet there has been nothing done to at least try remediating these as well. I can not explain how many times I have seen enemies clip through the map, usually while I am on an elevated surface suddenly rise from under the floor that I am on and kill me or end up getting stuck because a massive dead bile titan or impaler corpse left an invisible, impassable hitbox that seemingly takes forever to clear. For a development team to have earned so much money from this games massive success and continuously ignore critical, game-ruining bugs is absolutely devastating to see. It is especially infuriating as a player and person who owns this game to see how miserably slow and lazy the development team that allegedly has a group to fix these problems have it get even more damaged each major update with it taking months to fix what seemingly is simple bugs that have been shown that they are able to be fixed with modder creating mods that fixed these problems incredibly quickly.

I would also like to point out the choices that this development team has made for the game which always seems to go against everything that the players want. I recall one of the first major controversies this development team had done being the fact that they nerfed some of the weapons that were deemed too powerful. As a result this made the game a lot more unfair and harder than it previously was and with the array that we had at the time when players were still learning was brutal. I would completely understand this choice if this was not a PVE game. Which I constantly have myself seeing with many of these changes because frankly, they seem incredibly outlandish from a players perspective such as making the knockback radius of a war strider's grenade even larger, which can leave you stunlocked allowing for you to die without having a chance to fight back or stun you from areas that you would think you would be safe in which is mildly infuriating. Then with the change with hive gaurds armor pen being changed to heavy pen, which on later difficulties spawn just as much as the weaker enemies have high armor penetration. This was already outrageous as you would then need to use a gun or support weapon that would to kill them while having to deal with plenty of them already. Luckily this was reverted but it still confuses me as to why someone would decide that this was best for the fun of the players. As this would have likely forced people to either try to ignore them or be stuck using the same support weapons to ensure that they can deal with them which weapon variety is already a problem for the game as a lot of weapons that you get either have too niche of a use or are just completely useless against specific enemies which often had me using the same loadout every single match because nothing would compare and made the game so much more repetitive. Additionally with a lot of the weapons or armors that are incredibly helpful or fun to use are locked by warbonds which are about 10 dollars each and after paying for the game I do find it a bit bothersome that I can never enjoy the new content without having to pay for it or grind super credits for days. Even then they have shown that they can do interesting things with these warbonds like cosmetics and balancing the game like with the ironclad democracy warbond which when worn practically just reverted the explosion knock back changes that they have, selling us the solution of the communities complaints for ten dollars. 

Ultimately after everything that I have seen in the game and with the developers ignoring the playerbase time and time again I legitimately can not recommend this game to anyone as I feel like they would not be delivered the game that was shown to them and that I once fell in love with and played for hours 2 years ago.

Finally! I can leave a negative review from the UK. Took them long enough to get this MAJOR F-UP fixed.

With the lack of communication from the studio regarding their roadmap, the ongoing issues surrounding EAC, and the frankly ridiculous number of long-standing QoL problems, I feel like leaving a negative review is one of the few ways left to make our frustrations heard.

Whether the studio actually cares is another matter entirely. At this point, it feels like they're more interested in defending their decisions than acknowledging when those decisions have made the game worse.

Don't get me wrong. I enjoy Helldivers 2. That's precisely why I'm so frustrated with it. The potential for something genuinely fantastic is right there, constantly just out of reach because of problems that have persisted for months, sometimes well over a year. I want this game to succeed, but wanting it to improve doesn't mean I should have to excuse the decisions holding it back.

I don't need to rehash every problem with the game. A quick Google search will show you plenty of them, along with countless discussions from players who've been asking for solutions for over a year.

Balancing problems, inconsistent mechanics, stratagem bouncing, hellpod steering, and a whole host of other QoL issues. These aren't obscure complaints from a handful of players. They're recurring frustrations that the community has been raising for ages.

And here's what really gets me.

Modders managed to address many of these problems themselves. Some of those fixes were vibe-coded, but they worked. They improved the experience in ways players had been requesting for months. Then came the EAC changes and additional security measures, which effectively gutted those solutions.

So we're left with a rather stupid situation. Players demonstrated that improvements were possible, only to lose access to them while the underlying problems remained.

If someone can vibe-code a functional fix over a weekend, why can't an entire professional development studio deliver a proper, supported solution within a reasonable timeframe?

I'm not pretending that implementing, testing, and maintaining changes in a live-service game is as simple as throwing together a mod. It isn't. But that doesn't excuse the lack of progress, nor does it make the community's frustration any less justified.

I don't want Helldivers 2 to fail. I want it to be the game it so clearly has the potential to become.

But until the developers demonstrate that they're willing to address these long-standing issues, rather than simply expecting players to put up with them, I can't recommend it.

And if a negative review is what it takes to make that frustration visible, then so be it.

For those who just want the TLDR, Helldivers 2 is dying and this is due to Arrowhead's malicious laziness. 

But for many of you who want me to elaborate more on what I mean, I highly encourage everyone to carefully read through my current thoughts on this game as my opinion may change depending on which direction it goes from here. 

Ever since I started playing this game right around "Omens of Tyranny", I recognized right from the get-go that there was something special about this game that had me coming back for more each and every time. 

Despite its initial struggles and controversies, I still think that Helldivers 2 has a chance to go down as one of the greatest games in the modern day era, even going as far as being considered in some debates amongst the current gaming greats. 

However, I'm not sure when exactly, but something had changed about this game right around "Into the Unjust" and then fell apart right around the start of "Machinery of Oppression". 

And to see how everything unfolded after the installation of Easy Anti-Cheat, I could argue that this game is now officially dead or currently on life support as all I can say is that this was on Arrowhead for what they've done to this game. 

Based on everything I've seen, they have had many decisions that ended up leading into many domino effects in which it negatively affected both this game and the passionate players that love it so much. 

These decisions include many of the following but not limited to: 

- Terrible communication since Twinbeard's departure 

- Updates and patches becoming seasonal versus the initial 2 week period to improve the game they did 

- Hiding and lying about changes as noted by the Coyote nerf (Eroding trust & crippling fire based weapons)

- Use of false advertisement (Ex., Scope of Authority advertising & info from box cover for Helldivers 2) 

- Misleading messages (Unlocking a DSS Action vs initial description of a Stratagem Permit in a campaign reward) 

- No in-game explanation on key mechanics (Ex., Gambits, Sieges, & Planetary Decay) 

- No centralized platform to communicate (Discord, Reddit, and Twitter are the main platforms to communicate)

- Forcing certain stories and outcomes to occur like what happened in the Battle for Cyberstan 

- Cultivating a toxic community and turning it into a political mess (Ex., D10 Challenge Doxing Incident) 

- Devs abandoning the Illuminate (Cultists scrapped due to vibes and currently a mix of subfactions) 

- Enemies remaining over-tuned for years (Ex., War Strider & most of the available Illuminate units) 

- Enemies remaining buggy for long periods of time (Ex., Fleshmob clipping through walls and the ground) 

- Additional features that could've been added were scrapped (Customization for weapons, armor, and passives) 

- Issues taking years to address (Ex., Stratagem Bouncing & Hellpod Steering) 

- Creating a problem to sell a solution (Ex., Ragdoll increased so a Warbond has a passive that reduces ragdoll) 

- Banning mods due to these Modders doing a better job than Arrowhead themselves 

- New anti cheat has locked out a good amount of Linux and Xbox players from playing the game 
 
While this doesn't account for any other issues that Arrowhead has done to this game, the majority of the issues that many players have pointed out are constantly ignored by this AA company claiming to be a AAA studio. 

I don't know why this is the case but they seem to be so hellbent on having their "Grunt Fantasy" that they have been contradicting themselves at every turn, especially when it comes to their excuses on why Helldivers 2 can't have certain perks they know that everyone would like. 

These excuses and contradictions even include stuff like: 

- Invoking realism when it is only one sided (ex., Dragon Roach still flies even when its wings are gone) 

- Outdated Software (Darktide uses the same engine as HD2 but does it better, which is Autodesk Stingray) 

- Features not possible (Modders added so many perks that proved that Arrowhead can do it but wont) 

- Apple vs Bacon argument (Used to justify no armor customization despite the Malestrom existing) 

- Limits their design space (In other words, it limits the ways in which they can make more money off of us) 

- Claiming their player base is mostly Call of Duty players (Star Wars Battlefront 2 (2005) is where I came from) 

I think what makes it so sad is that Arrowhead Studios has the ability to get this done as long as they put in the effort, but they choose to not do any of it and always attempt to take the easy way out each and every time. 

This is honestly why I consider them to be "maliciously lazy" as they can put in the effort to fix all the known bugs, balance out the weapons, make the enemy factions feel good to fight against while still making it challenging but they refuse to do so and they choose to irritate everyone instead of doing their job. 

I think what also makes it worse is that they are apparently developing another game while Helldivers 2 is in such a poor state and if it goes the way that I expect they may be going down the same route as Bungie after what they did to Destiny 2 after introducing Marathon. 

But unlike Bungie which is going to do more for the Destiny franchise, it just seems like that they are going to bleed HD2 dry and then abandon it once they get their worth from it. 

And keep in mind, this is the same studio that mentioned that they wanted Helldivers 2 to last about 10 years or so and it doesn't even feel like that they will even make it pass Year 3 or Year 4 at all with the direction they are going. 

If they leave this game in such a horrible mess, its not going to matter how good their next game is as their players will do everything in their power to make sure that their next project fails. 

To be honest, it just feels like that the only way this can be addressed is for Sony to finally intervene on their work like they did before, even then I don't think we will see that happen due to Sony's most recent anti-consumer practices they have emphasized. 

And what makes this all the more ironic is their overall motto, "A game for everyone is a game for no one."

In other words, they have pretty much made a game I would argue is for no one now. 

Or in the case of how I would phrase it, "A game for no one is a game for no one." 

Like most of the players who hop onto this game, I still love it so much and want to see it succeed more than anything. 

But without honest critiques and developers/executives that are willing to listen to them, this game will keep going on an ongoing negative spiral that will drive away most players from ever coming back. 

It hurts so badly for me to say it, but I will not be recommending this game until significant changes are made that improve the current state of this game.

The 3 factions make it so that you get to devise a new set of gear that works for your playstyle and each new warbonds brings new ways to tweak your playstyle or toys that go along with that playstyle.

My biggest complaints:
The initial push for Sony to force account creation and linking, and then making it so that other countries couldn't play it after they had bought it.
That there needs to be new types of missions added regularly along with warbonds.  I haven't had but a couple problems that everyone is complaining about, but fixed.
There has been on occasion situations or updates that have added crashes or problems loading.  For me its been a few times.

REGARDING THE RECENT ANTICHEAT:  It has caused problems, even for me initially.  For my problem to launch the game after the update, which came 2 days after the update, was an error I could not pin down initially, [strike]but it turned out to be my ASUS armory crate programs, likely to be the RGB controller itself, but I'm unsure specifically which of the armory crate programs caused it.  I tried everything recommended, even reinstalling the game, and nothing worked until i removed armory crate software.  Now, I don't like that i have to remove legitimate software to play the game and that needs to be addressed, but perhaps this will help someone.[/strike]

HOWEVER, i do realize that the impact is smaller on a massive factor in PVE vs PVP, but it does not change the fact that cheating is cheating.  Only on a few occasions have I been impacted by cheaters that was bad enough that I and others noticed.  The most egregious cheat created an aura of damage from one player resulting in the highest team damage I've ever seen in this game.  A number that couldn't even be achieved if he had just dropped bombs on us the entire mission.  It's a problem because the cheat kept setting off hellbombs killing his teammates, constantly draining our life so we used up all our stims and would die when encountering enemies with additional damage occurring and no stims to heal.  This is quite annoying.  Also, cheating reporting is non existent.  The option is there but they only recommend blocking to handle cheating.  This prevents you from encountering the player again in matchmaking and that, ultimately is fine I guess.  I strongly dislike cheaters in ANY team environment.  Solo, fine, do whatever you want.  But the current decision to switch anti cheat software has caused more headaches and I don't know if that was worthwhile from a players perspective.
